legend: Given a tree[6]$$$^{[6]}$$$ of n$$$n$$$ vertices, find the lexicographically[2]$$$^{[2]}$$$ smallest string s$$$s$$$ that satisfies the following:
String s$$$s$$$ only consists of letters 'a', 'b', and 'c'.
For every edge (u,v)$$$(u,v)$$$ of the tree, su≠sv$$$s_u \neq s_v$$$.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — denoting the number of vertices in the tree.
Each of the following n−1$$$n - 1$$$ lines contains two integers u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ (1≤u,v≤n$$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$, u≠v$$$u \neq v$$$) — denoting the indices of the vertices connected by an edge.

output: Output a single line, containing a string of length n$$$n$$$ — the lexicographically smallest achievable string.
